title: Evaluating water quality and ecotoxicology assessment techniques using data from a lead and zinc effected upland limestone catchment
water_body: Hebden Beck catchment (16 sites: reservoir, main channel, perennial and ephemeral tributaries), Yorkshire Dales
alkalinity: DIC 0.9-42.7 mg/L (site means)
location_in_paper: WR 2017 Table 2 (annual mean dissolved and C_DGT, mol/L, 16 sites); site mean pH from ESPI 2017 SI Table 4-SI
notes: Computed by me: OLS of log10(site annual mean) on site mean pH; per-site means, not per-sample. DGT: Chelex, 0.8 mm APA diffusive gel + PES filter, 121 bimonthly deployments Dec 2013-Nov 2014 (18-43 d); water sampled monthly Nov 2013-Dec 2014. Spatial confounding: high-Zn sites are adit/spoil drainages at circumneutral pH with high Ca/DIC (limestone), while the two most acidic sites (H4 mean pH 3.9, H13 4.5) are peat-fed ephemeral tributaries with low metal loads and higher DOC; source strength, not pH, dominates. Individual pH values span 3.3-8.2. Chelex uptake of Zn may be suppressed at pH<5 (H+ competition) at H4/H13; authors did not correct. Pearson r. All 16 sites used.

title: Isotope geochemistry, hydrochemistry, and mineralogy of a river affected by acid mine drainage in a mining area, South China

location_in_paper: SI Tables S1 (pH), S3 (total Fe), S4 (Cu, Zn)
notes: Computed by me from SI Tables S1, S3, S4 (0.22 um filtered; FAAS). OLS of log10(dissolved, mg/L) on pH, all campaigns pooled. Zero/missing values excluded.
